text:
kevin: Heads up — we're seeing packet loss / high retransmits between GPU nodes in us-west-2 that started ~08:10 UTC. Affected pods are in the ml-gpu namespace.

maya: noticed the same on perf tests, iperf shows 20-30% retransmit on 10G links.

rachel: is this across AZs or intra-AZ?

kevin: mostly intra-AZ but between different nodes (same subnet). latency spikes and packet loss when we run CUDA inference load.

jose: any recent networkpolicy changes in ml-gpu? last deploy changed default egress deny + a policy that allowed CIDRs only.

kevin: yes — someone replaced a permissive egress rule with CIDR-based allowlists. That blocks pod-to-pod traffic that relied on namespace selectors.

maya: that matches: when I exec'd into a gpu pod and ping another pod IP it fails. But localhost and host-networked pods are fine.

rachel: can you paste the policy?

kevin: here — from gitops (sanitized):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-egress-lockdown
  namespace: ml-gpu
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 443
```

kevin: basically they allowed only 443 to the world, nothing else — so intra-cluster pod traffic (pod IPs) is implicitly blocked.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-47. Assigned to @oncall.

jose: That policy is wrong for our setup. We rely on namespaceSelector-based egress for intra-cluster control. Also GPU workloads use RDMA (RoCE v2) for GPUDirect and some components use UDP port 4791 — that will be blocked by the TCP-only port rule.

maya: interesting — our RDMA flows were showing huge packet drops in tcpdump: lots of UDP retransmits. ethtool stats show Rx errors increasing. Could be MTU mismatch plus policy drop.

rachel: what's the MTU on the nodes?

maya: on the affected nodes: ip link show dev eth0 -> mtu 1500; but our SR-IOV/host devices expect 9000 for RDMA.

kevin: so two issues stacked: networkpolicy blocking pod-to-pod egress + MTU mismatch causing fragmentation/loss for jumbo frame traffic.

jose: steps I ran:
1) kubectl -n ml-gpu get networkpolicies
2) kubectl exec -it pod/gpu-1 -- ping -c3 10.244.5.12 (failed)
3) kubectl exec -it pod/gpu-1 -- iperf3 -c 10.244.5.12 -> 25% retransmits
4) tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp port 4791 -> saw truncated frames

kevin: tried a quick workaround: patched policy to add an egress rule with namespaceSelector and UDP/TCP for intra-cluster traffic. applied as a hotfix.

kevin: patch I applied:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-allow-intra
  namespace: ml-gpu
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          team: ml
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 4791
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 22
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9090
```

maya: after that intra-pod ping mostly worked but we still saw some packet loss for big transfers.

rachel: that points back to MTU. If the calico or CNI overlay is set to 1500 and host NICs are 9000, fragmentation can cause drops, especially for RDMA/UDP.

jose: confirmed: kube-proxy iptables rules show no weirdness. CNI (calico) IPIP mode was on with MTU 1440. Host NIC was set to 9000 so jumbo frames get fragmented on encapsulation.

kevin: recommended mitigation: set CNI MTU to 9000 across nodes or force RoCE to use path MTU discovery-friendly settings. For now we rolled back the CIDR-only policy and restored namespaceSelector-based egress + added explicit UDP 4791 allow.

ops-bot: rollback applied for networkpolicy ml-egress-lockdown at 1748001256 by kevin.

maya: action items:
- short: ensure networkpolicy allows intra-namespace/selected namespaces for UDP 4791 and other critical ports (done hotfix)
- medium: sync CNI MTU with host NICs, update gitops CNI config across cluster (jira: INF-912)
- long: add a pre-deploy test that runs iperf and RDMA smoke checks for ml-gpu namespace and validate networkpolicy YAML via a linter that flags CIDR-only egress in namespaces that have internal pod mesh.

rachel: also add monitoring alert: pod-to-pod packet loss rate > 5% for 5m -> page infra oncall.

jose: I'll open a PR to update gitops networkpolicy to use namespaceSelector and add the RDMA UDP port, and include a note about MTU.

kevin: thanks everyone. tagging @security — we need to ensure we're not widening egress too much when we revert. We'll scope to in-cluster namespaces only.

infra-bot: lint-check failed on PR #428: networkpolicy missing explicit port ranges.

kevin: noted — will iterate. For now the cluster is stable for ML inference. Continuing postmortem to include timeline and the gitops diff that caused the regression.

jose: paste of quick commands used for debugging:
- kubectl -n ml-gpu get pods -o wide
- kubectl exec -n ml-gpu -it pod/gpu-1 -- iperf3 -c 10.244.5.12 -t 10
- sudo ethtool -k eth0
- ip -s link show dev eth0
- sudo tc qdisc show dev eth0
- calicoctl get ippool -o yaml

maya: saving tcpdump and iperf logs to S3: s3://redwood-debug/ml-gpu/1748001234/

kevin: will draft postmortem and add mitigation checklist.

rachel: great. closing thread once postmortem linked.
